Credit-claiming is when a senator takes credit for something - a policy achievement, funding secured, legislation passed, benefits delivered to constituents. The classic Mayhew definition: acting so as to generate a belief in a relevant political actor (or actors) that one is personally responsible for causing the government, or some unit thereof, to do something that the actor considers desirable.

Key indicators:
- "Senator X announced federal funding for..."
- "Senator X secured $Y for..."
- "I helped secure..."
- "My amendment/provision passed..."
- Taking credit for grants, projects, designations
- "I authored legislation that..."

Not credit-claiming:
- Position-taking (statements on issues, votes explained without claiming causal credit)
- Just announcing funding without claiming role (though typically senators announcing grants is considered credit-claiming even if implicit - in congressional literature, "Senator X announced that [local entity] received a grant" is generally coded as credit-claiming because the announcement itself implies responsibility)
